claim_text: Defang says an attacker got into its build system and copied the credentials it uses to run Defang
summary: Defang says: 'On November 12, 2026 an attacker got into the Defang Deploy build system and copied the credentials we use to run Defang.' With them, it says, the attacker downloaded a copy of its main database.
detail: Defang says it confirmed this on Nov 23, 2026, 11 days later, after a routine security scan found suspicious activity in its repositories, and published its post on Nov 24.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Defang's own incident post states it.

claim_text: The attacker acted as a Defang GitHub App used for testing, and production trusted the release it tagged
summary: Defang says a separate GitHub App it used for development had more permissions than it needed. Acting as that app, the attacker pushed a commit, tagged it as a release, and production ran it with access to production credentials.
detail: Defang says the app was installed on two of its own repositories and could change deployment environments. 'Our production environment trusted release tags, so their code ran in our CI with access to our production credentials.' It has revoked the app's credentials and suspended it.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Defang's post describes the route in.

claim_text: Who did it is not known
summary: Defang does not name an attacker, and we found no claim of responsibility. Defang does not say how the attacker came to act as its development app.
detail: We did not open leak or dark-web sites.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: The post names no attacker and does not explain the first step.

claim_text: Whether the stolen credentials were used after Nov 12 is not known
summary: Defang says the credentials stayed valid until it replaced them on Nov 23 and that it is still checking whether they were used after Nov 12. 'Some of our logs are not detailed enough to rule that out.'
detail: Defang says it will update its post when it knows more. It says it has notified GitHub, which is helping it check for misuse of the tokens.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: Defang says it does not yet know.

claim_text: Defang's main database was copied, with every Defang Portal account in it
summary: Defang says names, email addresses, GitHub or GitLab usernames and organisation names, sign-up answers, connected cloud account IDs and deployed Compose files were copied. Everyone with a Defang Portal account is in it.
detail: For users who installed the Defang GitHub App, the names of the repositories it can reach, including private ones, were also copied. Defang says its timeline puts the database copy at 07:57 to 08:10 UTC on Nov 12.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Defang's post lists what was taken.

claim_text: Saved copies of deployments from Oct 12 to Nov 19 were taken, and can include database passwords
summary: Defang says copies of deployment state from deploys between Oct 12 and Nov 19 were taken. These 'can include database passwords' and environment variables built from Defang config values.
detail: Defang says it stopped keeping these copies on Nov 19 and deleted the ones it had.
label: Confirmed

claim_text: The key to the Defang GitHub App and customers' GitHub sign-in tokens were taken
summary: Defang says the attacker could use the app's key and the GitHub tokens it stores. The tokens were encrypted, but the encryption key was taken too. Until Nov 23 they could act in customers' repositories as the app.
detail: Defang lists what that allows: pushing commits, changing workflow files, overwriting Actions secrets, changing deployment environments and repository settings, and merging pull requests. It says a workflow started this way can receive the customer's cloud credentials, because the deploy role Defang set up trusts workflows in the repository.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Defang's post states what the attacker held.

claim_text: A payment-provider key was taken, which could read billing records but not full card numbers
summary: Defang says a key for its Stripe account was copied. Until Nov 23 it could read billing names and addresses, tax IDs, card brand, last four digits and expiry, and invoice history. Full card numbers and security codes were not exposed.
detail: Defang says customers do not need to replace their card.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Defang's post lists what the key could read.

claim_text: Defang says no passwords, cloud credentials or repository contents were exposed
summary: Defang says it holds no passwords (sign-in is through GitHub, GitLab or an emailed code), never holds customers' cloud credentials, and does not store repository contents. Nobody outside Defang has checked.
detail: It names one indirect path to a customer's cloud account: the GitHub Actions deploy role, through the GitHub App credentials (c007).
label: Reported
why_it_supports: The company's own statement. No outside check has been published, so Reported.

claim_text: Defang replaced its credentials on Nov 23, signed everyone out and emailed affected users
summary: Defang says it replaced the GitHub App key and its other production credentials on Nov 23, revoked stored GitHub tokens, signed out every session, emailed every affected user, and notified GitHub and the relevant authorities.
detail: It also says it cancelled pending cloud invite links, reverted deployment settings the attacker had changed, and installed a security update to a dependency on Nov 15. It does not say whether that update is connected to the breach.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Defang's post lists what it has done.

claim_text: Defang asks GitHub App users to check their repositories and cloud accounts, and some users to change secrets
summary: Defang asks users of its GitHub App to look for activity they did not start since Nov 11 and to lock down its deploy environments. Anyone who deployed between Oct 12 and Nov 19 should change database passwords and secrets.
detail: Defang's post gives step-by-step checks for GitHub, AWS, Google Cloud and Azure. Everyone will need to sign in to Defang again.
label: Confirmed

claim_text: Whether this is connected to the 1Password and Todoist breaches the same week
summary: Commenters on Hacker News point out that this, 1Password's and Todoist's breaches all went through GitHub access. None of the three companies has linked them, and we found no source that does.
detail: The routes differ as each company tells it: Defang's own development GitHub App, a 1Password employee's GitHub account, and a stolen credential for Todoist's code system. The Hacker News discussion is cited only as where the question is raised.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: No source links the three; the question comes from commenters with no stated knowledge.

claim_text: Which organisations use Defang, and whether any were affected, is not publicly known
summary: Defang's site names no customers, and no organisation has said publicly that it uses Defang or that it was affected. Defang says it has emailed every affected user.
detail: Defang's home page lists business partners and cloud providers under 'Our Partners'. A partner is not a customer, and none has said it was affected, so they are not named here. The organisations most at risk are those that installed the Defang GitHub App and deploy from GitHub Actions (c007).
label: Not established
why_it_supports: Defang's own site names no customers, and its post names none.
